title: Diagnosing and Mitigating Modality Interference in Multimodal Large Language Models
reasoning: The paper focuses on the technical challenges of modality interference in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), specifically how task-irrelevant signals from one modality can distort predictions. It evaluates model performance on standard vision and language benchmarks like Mini-ImageNet, MMLU, and ScienceQA. It contains no evaluation or benchmarking related to religion, faith, spiritual traditions, morals, or ethics.
